atlasValidation: Every sprite in manifest must have generated file/atlas region before release; no arbitrary missing icons
lookRules: Vivid but readable original tropical pixel art, no emoji-based final gameplay assets
Named assets keep consistent scale and 4-direction character anchoring
Canvas procedural art may create source sprites but must export/cache images once; avoid per-frame detailed primitives
At home doorway, roof fades and furniture visible without changing scene
Night lights and water animation optional quality setting, never hidden gameplay requirement

mandatoryAssets.itemIcons: 179 unique canonical itemId bindings, iconKey exact
mandatoryAssets.buildings: 58 building ids, at least ghost/complete; prefab houses interior/roof/construction stages
mandatoryAssets.wildlife: 25 species ids with visible idle/move/react where applicable
mandatoryAssets.crops: 12 species each 4 stages; wet/dry overlay tint can be reused
mandatoryAssets.character: 16 clips at declared frame sizes, all directions in ArtSpec; coherent layers
mandatoryAssets.terrain: 20 terrain categories, transitions, river/ocean borders, collision and elevation indicators
mandatoryAssets.effects: fire, chop/mine impact, rain, tide, underwater visibility, hit and healing, water glint
mandatoryAssets.ui: touch joystick, contextual action, quickbar6, 9 menu entry icons, readable all panels

preReleaseAssetAudit: All referenced asset files physically exist in build output, or are explicit sprites in bundled atlas
No missing texture error from fresh cache
No icon drawn solely as unicode emoji in shipped UI
All 38 POI visual identities match POIDB, not legacy POI_01 order
Character animations do not detach tools from hand
Low quality mode removes only ambience, not gameplay visibility
